title: Deciphering the Biocontrol and Plant-Growth-Promoting Potential of a Rhizobacterium, Streptomyces cavourensis SAI-25, Using Whole Genome Sequence and In-Vitro Assays
content: A rice rhizosphere Streptomyces strain SAI-25 was previously reported to exhibit biocontrol activity against a limited range of agricultural pests, leaving its broader agricultural potential unexplored. In this study, we have combined whole genome sequencing with untargeted metabolomics, and in vitro assays to examine its full agricultural potential. Genome similarity reassigned SAI-25 as a putative new strain of S. cavourensis. The comparative genome analysis and genome annotation revealed the presence of several unique protein-coding genes with putative functions majorly associated with adaptation to the surrounding, highlighting its genomic novelty. Among the predicted Biosynthetic Gene Clusters (BGCs) for secondary metabolites, the majority were annotated as having biocontrol and plant growth-promoting (PGP) activities. In addition to one of this annotated BGC (valinomycin, a broad spectrum antimicrobial compound), few additional agriculturally relevant metabolites were also detected through public spectral library matching. For the previously reported insecticidal diketopiperazine derivative produced by SAI-25, one candidate BGC capable of its biosynthesis was predicted. Finally, the in-vitro assays revealed its broad range of PGP activities. Overall, the SAI-25’s versatile secondary metabolites and potent PGP enzymes highlight its potential as a promising biopesticide/biofertilizer candidate.
